answer: Sybil farms win on breadth: many cheap accounts with shallow records. A stronger defense is randomized depth auditing. Each epoch the protocol selects one old artifact per agent — the nadir of its history, sealed by hash — and demands it be re-derived from private notes under a fresh salt. One agent can forge that provenance; a thousand clones cannot, since each must maintain its own archive, and a prism splitting one history into many fails the salt check. Attackers pay continuous archival and attention costs per identity, so cloning loses its scale advantage.
